label: PF Backlog 223
title: Backend: two-phase feasibility & capability triage - BUILD-HOST at ideation (now) + DESTINATION runtime at packaging (later); go/conditional/no-go + delivery mode
body:
## Problem / why
Today a project can enter design/architecture and only LATER discover that: a required modality has no
generator, the needed weights are not shippable, the BUILD host (the machine running Product Forge) cannot
run the model locally, the DESTINATION system (where the product will run) cannot run it either, or the
cost blows the budget. We need this known early - build feasibility AT IDEATION, run feasibility LATER.

## Goal & value
A **two-phase feasibility & capability triage**:
- **Phase 1 - BUILD-HOST (MANDATORY, at ideation):** profile the machine that is BUILDING the product (this
  host) and decide, per modality, whether it can be built locally or must use API.
- **Phase 2 - DESTINATION (DEFERRED, after the product is built / at packaging):** profile the system where
  the PRODUCT will RUN and decide how it ships (bundle weights vs API/BYOK vs hosted vs hybrid).

## Phase 1 - build-host feasibility (at ideation)
- **Hardware probe** of the current host: GPU model + **VRAM**, RAM, free disk, (CUDA/CPU only).
- For each required modality/kind: can THIS host run the needed model(s) locally (incl. quantized)?
  Else the build path must use API for that modality.
- Decide **build-mode per modality**: local | API | aggregator.
- Verdict at ideation: **go | conditional | no-go** (e.g. "video not local -> conditional: API required").

## Phase 2 - destination/runtime feasibility (later, after build)
- Profile the **target system** where the product runs: end-user device tier (GPU/CPU/none), server, or your
  cloud; plus expected volume.
- Decide **shipping mode**: local (bundle weights) | API (BYOK) | hosted | hybrid; pick the SKU
  (offline-weights vs thin-API).
- List required hardware / API keys for the end user.

## Shared dimensions (both phases)
- Capability exists (catalog generator; `core/modality.generators_needed()`),
- License / `bundle_allowed` (restricted -> API-only or exclude),
- Cost projection vs budget (BI-0194), free/paid mix,
- Data/privacy/residency + safety/moderation, latency/UX.

## Outputs
- `products/<project>/feasibility.json` (single writer; register in store-registry.json) with TWO sections:
  `build` (phase 1, filled at ideation) and `runtime` (phase 2, filled later).
- Human report; risks + mitigations; required hardware/keys; consumed by design/architect (phase 1) and by
  packaging/release (phase 2).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- At IDEATION, the gate reports which modalities THIS build host can do locally vs needs API - before design.
- An idea needing video on a CPU-only/4GB build host is flagged "conditional: API required" up front.
- A restricted weight (e.g. FLUX.1-dev) is flagged "API-only / not shippable".
- AFTER the build, a second pass profiles the destination and sets the shipping mode (bundle vs API vs
  hosted) WITHOUT redoing phase 1 (idempotent; phase 2 can run later).
- Persisted + surfaced to the right stage at the right time.

## Verification / test plan
- Unit: build-host decision matrix (idea x host profile) at ideation; destination matrix (target profile)
  at packaging.
- Integration: app idea (go) vs video-only-on-CPU (conditional API) vs restricted weight (API-only);
  later destination pass selects shipping mode.

## Dependencies & links
BI-0210, BI-0192, BI-0194, BI-0206, BI-0207, BI-0213. See docs/tools-and-generators.md (SS21 policy) and
docs/multimodel_architecture_support.md.
